label: DFSM Interval Example
info:
Demonstrates config-owned interval scheduling with skip and queue_one policies.

The dfsm-state-machine owns the periodic active-lifecycle emissions.
Interval emissions are lifecycle signals (lifecycleType = "active_interval"), not state transitions or retriggers.

An active cycle resolves only on a real state-changing accepted transition.
Same-state retrigger requests do NOT resolve the cycle.

Policy behavior:
  skip      - interval ticks that arrive while a cycle is in-flight are silently dropped.
  queue_one - at most one pending emission is held; it is delivered on real cycle resolution if the state is unchanged.

name: Interval scheduling owned by dfsm-state-machine. Policy: skip (fixed_rate, 2s).
info:
The dfsm-state-machine config node owns the interval timer.
dfsm-active subscribes to active-lifecycle emissions which include both
transition snapshots (lifecycleType=active_transition) and periodic
interval signals (lifecycleType=active_interval).

An in-flight cycle is started when a transition or interval emission is dispatched.
With 'skip' policy, interval ticks that fire while a cycle is unresolved are dropped.
The cycle resolves only when a state-changing transition is accepted.

To see queue_one behavior, change intervalPolicy to 'queue_one' on the config node.

name: All lifecycle emissions: transition and periodic interval signals
Classify lifecycle emission
RUNNING state handler — receives transition + interval emissions for RUNNING only
info:
With skip policy and 2s interval:
- First emission is the accepted transition (lifecycleType=active_transition, changed=true).
- The cycle is now in-flight/unresolved.
- Interval ticks fire every 2s but are skipped because a cycle is unresolved.
- The cycle resolves when the next state-changing transition is accepted.

With queue_one policy:
- The first interval tick that fires while in-flight is queued (queuedIntervalEmission=true).
- Additional ticks while unresolved are coalesced (only one remains queued).
- On cycle resolution (state changes), the queued emission is delivered if the resolved state matches.

name: RUNNING handler
Resolution semantics: cycle clears on state-changing transitions only
info:
An active cycle starts when a transition snapshot or interval signal is dispatched to dfsm-active.
It resolves only when a later accepted dfsm-activate request causes a real state change.

Same-state retrigger requests do NOT resolve the cycle:
  - They emit an active_transition snapshot with changed=false, retrigger=true.
  - inFlightUnresolved stays true.
  - Interval ticks continue to be skipped (skip) or coalesced (queue_one).

Interval emissions are lifecycle signals, not transitions:
  - They carry lifecycleType='active_interval'.
  - They do not advance eventId.
  - They do not mutate transition state (changed, retrigger, eventId).
  - They are not same-state retriggers.
